svg.title: Convert a Defined Account Cohort
svg.desc: diagram id: diag-02-qualified-account-conversion; chart type: funnel; title: Convert a Defined Account Cohort; subtitle: One hundred target accounts narrow to five signed service accounts.; chapter number: 6; epistemic tag: illustrative_model; assumptions note: Illustrative counts follow one account cohort across a complete sales cycle; they are not observed conversion benchmarks. Every later stage is a subset of the preceding stage. First-deal planning remains 2–5 months, not one sprint.; caption: Count accounts consistently: route reviews, proposals, and awards refer to the same original account list.; stages: label: Mapped target accounts; value: 100 accounts with named purchasing or transport contacts; numeric value: 100.0; detail: Build a deduplicated list of Medicaid transport brokers, workers'-comp administrators, laboratories, and collection networks within the service territory.; label: Qualified service fit; value: 60 accounts pass territory, service, and payer screening; numeric value: 60.0; detail: Retain 60% of the original cohort after confirming outsourcing demand, procurement access, credentialing requirements, and feasible payment terms.; label: Documented route discovery; value: 30 accounts share usable service and exception requirements; numeric value: 30.0; detail: Advance 50% of qualified accounts after receiving trip windows, route density, transport levels, specimen needs, or other service-specific workload evidence.; label: Costed proposals delivered; value: 15 accounts receive capacity-backed pricing and service terms; numeric value: 15.0; detail: Advance 50% of discovery accounts after pricing driver settlements, deadhead, standby coverage, failed pickups, and collection timing.; label: Signed service accounts; value: 5 accounts execute scoped contracts with operating contacts; numeric value: 5.0; detail: Convert one-third of proposals and 5% of the original cohort. Signing does not equal dispatch readiness, recognized revenue, or collected cash.

rect.title: label: Mapped target accounts; value: 100 accounts with named purchasing or transport contacts; numeric value: 100.0; detail: Build a deduplicated list of Medicaid transport brokers, workers'-comp administrators, laboratories, and collection networks within the service territory.

label: Qualified service fit; value: 60 accounts pass territory, service, and payer screening; numeric value: 60.0; detail: Retain 60% of the original cohort after confirming outsourcing demand, procurement access, credentialing requirements, and feasible payment terms.

label: Documented route discovery; value: 30 accounts share usable service and exception requirements; numeric value: 30.0; detail: Advance 50% of qualified accounts after receiving trip windows, route density, transport levels, specimen needs, or other service-specific workload evidence.

label: Costed proposals delivered; value: 15 accounts receive capacity-backed pricing and service terms; numeric value: 15.0; detail: Advance 50% of discovery accounts after pricing driver settlements, deadhead, standby coverage, failed pickups, and collection timing.

label: Signed service accounts; value: 5 accounts execute scoped contracts with operating contacts; numeric value: 5.0; detail: Convert one-third of proposals and 5% of the original cohort. Signing does not equal dispatch readiness, recognized revenue, or collected cash.

text.title: Assumptions: Illustrative counts follow one account cohort across a complete sales cycle; they are not observed conversion benchmarks. Every later stage is a subset of the preceding stage. First-deal planning remains 2–5 months, not one sprint.
text.tspan: Assumptions: Illustrative counts follow one account cohort across a complete sales cycle; they are not observed conversion
benchmarks. Every later stage is a subset of the preceding stage. First-deal planning remains 2–5 months, not one sprint.

text.title: Stage widths/positions share a zero baseline; negative counts are unavailable.
